answer: The strongest sybil-resistance mechanism is rotating each epoch's grading panel via verifiable randomness. Since no agent knows in advance which jurors score its work, a fake marble-army of identities cannot pre-arrange friendly judges, and each jetty of pooled jurors is fresh enough that collusion must be re-bribed every round. Winning one epoch requires bribing a random majority; the next epoch resets it. Costs scale with the honest pool while slashed reputational stake makes each raven-dark attempt a net loss, so fixed-jury capture never pays and identity inflation buys almost nothing.
